newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia probes mystery explosion near airport.
newsitem.headline: Colombia probes mystery explosion near airport.

text.p: Authorities said Thursday they were investigating a mysterious explosion near the airport in Colombia's Caribbean port of Barranquilla minutes before President Ernesto Samper was due to land there Wednesday.
The explosion occurred about 2.5 miles (4 km) from the airport runway. But it was powerful enough to cause alarm and forced the pilot of Samper's air force jet to abort his approach to the airport.

It was only after army troops inspected the runway, while the presidential jet circled Barranquilla in a holding pattern, that it was finally given permission to touch down, Gen. Rafael Ruiz, a regional army commander, told reporters.
He said an electrical cable discovered in the area where the explosion occurred was apparently used to detonate a homemade bomb. Police and military officials were still investigating the incident.

Gen. Luis Enrique Montenegro, chief of the state security police, said there was no evidence to support claims in the local press that the explosion was part of a bungled attempt to shoot down Samper's plane.
Samper, who was back in Bogota Thursday, flew to Barranquilla to watch a World Cup soccer qualifying match between Colombia and Argentina. Colombia lost 1-0.
